input: The driver calls yesterday's event a brief blank spell rather than a blackout: while seated after a delivery he stopped answering for roughly 20 seconds and cannot remember his colleague moving the cup from his hand, although he did not fall and denies having lost consciousness; the colleague describes an unresponsive stare, and whether awareness was actually lost remains uncertain.

A similar episode may have occurred ten days earlier, but dates and duration are unclear; the referral mentions a possible rhythm disturbance, seizure or sleep-related event without a confirmed diagnosis, and both ambulatory cardiac monitoring and neurological review are pending, so neither a benign cause nor a recurrence-free interval has been established.

The initial form says No blackouts, but during further questioning the driver reports a blackout while queuing in the heat six weeks ago and describes a second collapse the following week; he recovered quickly, says someone suggested a faint, and has not been told by a treating clinician that either event was definitively vasovagal syncope.

The driver was diagnosed with type 2 diabetes several years ago and says the old diet-only label is no longer correct because he now injects insulin each evening, although he cannot name the preparation or dose; after skipping lunch last week he became sweaty and confused in the depot, and a colleague had to bring a sweet drink because he could not organise it himself.

A glucose value of 3.1 mmol/L was recorded only after he started drinking, he denies having passed out, and there is no contemporaneous clinical assessment confirming how severe the episode was; he also describes occasions when the sensor alarm sounded before he noticed symptoms, has not brought three months of monitoring records, and is waiting for endocrinology review.

There is a family history of diabetes in the driver's mother, but he says nobody has diagnosed him; over the last fortnight he has been unusually thirsty, getting up several times at night to pass urine and noticing intermittent blur after long shifts, while a borrowed meter displayed 17.8 mmol/L once without a verified testing protocol or confirmatory laboratory result.
